It also needs durable per-principal preference memory: meeting-type defaults, buffer rules, which days a partner protects, who is a VIP worth double-booking around, how a given candidate or client prefers to be contacted, and the outcome of past coordination with that same person. In executive recruiting the same candidates and hiring managers recur across searches, so remembering prior interactions is what separates it from a booking link. agents: Deep and first-party. Raycast AI ships: Agents (persistent, reusable AI personas that carry a system prompt, a chosen model, an icon and a scoped tool set across conversations — a built-in 'Deep Research' agent ships as a template, and agents can be shared across an org); AI Extensions (natural-language commands that drive OS functions and third-party apps as tools); Skills (reusable instructions and knowledge auto-discovered based on message content); MCP server support for connecting external tools; Screen Awareness (ask AI about what is on screen); Quick AI; 30+ AI Commands; and access to 30+ models across OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity and DeepSeek, plus local models and bring-your-own-keys. Notably, their docs describe Agents as scoped conversation personas rather than autonomous long-running workers — memory is described as within-chat, not persistent across agent runs.
why_memory: Strongest category fit of the three — but with a large caveat: they already built it themselves. Raycast Pro explicitly ships 'Memory' and 'Profile' as personalization features. Per manual.raycast.com/ai/personalization, Profile is manually curated user context (role, coding preferences, communication style) and Memory is described as 'A summary that Raycast AI automatically builds from your conversations over time' — a background job that collects recent AI Chat and Quick AI conversations every few hours, sends them to a model, and writes an updated user summary that is user-viewable, user-editable, disableable, encrypted at rest via Cloud Sync, and never used for training. That is precisely the product an agent-memory vendor sells. So Raycast is the archetypal buyer profile (multi-session AI assistant, per-user personalization, cross-device sync, privacy constraints, enterprise governance needs) and simultaneously the archetypal build-not-buy risk. A Honcho logo here reads much more like an individual Raycast developer trying Honcho than like Raycast outsourcing its memory layer.
sells_to: Prosumer and developer-first, expanding into B2B. Individuals (free / $10 Pro), teams ($15/user Pro), and enterprise (custom, with SAML and admin governance). Buyers are engineers, designers and knowledge workers; enterprise motion is bottom-up from individual adoption.
